job.value: Send a service request with details to the chosen provider(s)

arrivedFrom.value: 'Select for quote' on the Home Assistant results

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: The 'Service enquiry' title, 'Pick a service' and 'Service details' fields and 'Send request' button make the purpose clear.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: 'Send request' is the only full-width button but it shows disabled, and the empty 'Pick a service' field has no placeholder or chevron saying it is tappable.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'Send request' predicts its outcome, but the 'Pick a service' box gives no hint whether it's a dropdown or free text, and the refresh icon top-right has no label.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: Terms like 'Service details', 'number of units' and 'Furniture assembly' are everyday words.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: The person knows their problem, but the placeholder 'e.g. my  has been having issues' has a missing word, so the example they're meant to follow is broken.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: 'Other issues (Optional)' is clearly marked optional and kept below the required fields.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: Every field is about describing the job for a provider, which fits a pre-quote enquiry.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: One helper line under 'Service details'; the rest is labels and checkboxes.
